claims.text: The starting material is an equiatomic Nb-Ti-V-Zr-Hf high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast starting alloy is a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
Increasing hydrostatic pressure will contract the alloy lattice.
Pressure-induced lattice contraction modifies interatomic distances.
The altered interatomic distances modify the electronic band structure.
The altered interatomic distances modify the phonon spectrum.
Decreasing interatomic distances under pressure increases the effective density of states at the Fermi level.
Decreasing interatomic distances under pressure stiffens phonon modes.
The proposed electronic and phonon changes enhance electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling favors Cooper-pair formation and the emergence of superconductivity.
The alloy will begin to exhibit superconductivity at a critical pressure.
Pressure-induced superconductivity will produce a pronounced resistivity drop and an onset of diamagnetic AC susceptibility.
The superconducting transition temperature will increase systematically with further pressure while the alloy remains homogeneous and single phase.
At ambient pressure, the as-cast alloy is expected to show no superconducting transition or a significantly lower transition temperature.
The proposed pressure mechanism is limited to conditions in which pressure is uniform and the alloy remains a homogeneous single phase.
Nonhydrostatic loading or pressures that compromise structural integrity could cause competing effects or phase transitions.
Local pressure inhomogeneity may reduce the reproducibility and clarity of the superconducting transition.
The proposed test applies pressure from ambient conditions to several gigapascals and measures resistivity and AC susceptibility down to 1.8 K at each pressure.
